lead: Why bigger telescopes see sharper: the bigger the mirror, the finer the detail it can make out.
try: Move the sliders for colour and separation, and watch two stars blur together or split apart.
points: Light spreads out a little as it enters a telescope. A bigger mirror spreads it less, so the picture is sharper.
Hubble sees far finer detail than your eye, but even it cannot see the flags left on the Moon.
Webb sees heat light (infrared), so it must be kept very cold, or its own warmth would blind it.
